faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for a person to be complicit in an offense. A person is legally
               accountable as principal for the behavior of another constituting a criminal offense
               if, with the intent to promote or facilitate the commission of an offense, he or she
               aids, abets, advises, or encourages the other person in planning or committing the
               offense.
(b)
Criminal complicity shall be punishable by a fine or imprisonment not to exceed the
               limits established in
section 1-5
, except that if a person is found complicit in a non-jailable offense, that complicity
               shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed the limits established in
section 1-5
.
(
Ord. No. 4076, § 1, 7-16-2007
)
